title: Create an Accessible Animation Toggle
description: Build a button that switches between full motion and reduced motion, persisting preference.
problemStatement:
## Motion Preference Toggle

Create a small interactive demo with a button and a bouncing box animation. The page should:

1. Respect the user's OS‑level `prefers-reduced-motion` setting by default.
2. Show a toggle button labelled "Reduce motion" / "Enable motion" that overrides the OS preference for this session.
3. Use CSS custom properties to control animation duration.
4. Use `localStorage` to persist the user's choice.

Build the HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The animation itself can be a simple CSS keyframe that bounces a square up and down.
hints: Use `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` to detect OS preference initially.
Toggle a class on the body to switch between motion states.
expectedOutput: A working webpage where the toggle button immediately stops or starts the animation and remembers the choice on reload.
solutionCode: /* CSS */ :root { --duration: 2s; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { :root { --duration: 0s; } } .reduced-motion { --duration: 0s !important; } .box { width: 50px; height: 50px; background: rebeccapurple; animation: bounce var(--duration) infinite alternate; } @keyframes bounce { from { transform: translateY(0); } to { transform: translateY(100px); } } // JS const btn = document.getElementById('toggle-motion'); const prefersReduced = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'); let motionPref = localStorage.getItem('motion') || (prefersReduced.matches ? 'off' : 'on'); function applyMotion() { if (motionPref === 'off') { document.body.classList.add('reduced-motion'); btn.textContent = 'Enable motion'; } else { document.body.classList.remove('reduced-motion'); btn.textContent = 'Reduce motion'; } } applyMotion(); btn.addEventListener('click', () => { motionPref = motionPref === 'on' ? 'off' : 'on'; localStorage.setItem('motion', motionPref); applyMotion(); });
